title: Stream Fence: adaptive ingest gateway with contract linter and graceful leniency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: implement a front-line ingestion component (Stream Fence) that performs adaptive, low-latency contract linting for usage events destined for the Console analytics pipeline. Goals: fail fast for high-confidence contract violations, apply progressive leniency for marginal schema drift, and provide rich rejection reasons + remediation hints back to clients. This reduces downstream pipeline errors, cut alert noise, and enables proactive schema evolution workflows.

Why this work: current ingest nodes frequently either accept wildly malformed payloads (causing backfill and expensive downstream fixes) or reject too aggressively (causing customer errors and support tickets). Stream Fence will strike a pragmatic trade-off: protect the pipeline while minimizing false positives and providing operators actionable telemetry.

Non-goals: full schema evolution governance UI (handled by separate PM work), user-facing SDK changes, or large-scale reingestion tooling (backfills handled by dedicated jobs).
acceptance_criteria:
- New ingest gateway validates 100% of events for configured contracts before entering main pipeline.
- High-confidence violations return 4xx with structured error payload and guidance link.
- 'Lenient mode' accepts events with tagged deviations and attaches _schema_deviation metadata for downstream processing.
- End-to-end ingestion latency (gateway + validation) P95 < 120ms under steady-state 500 rps per instance.
- False positive rejection rate < 1% on recent production sample set.
- Observability: dashboard with rejection reasons, rate of lenient accept, and SLA heatmap is published.
- Security review completed for the WASM sandbox and signer integration.
technical_approach:
High level: build Stream Fence as a horizontally scalable microservice sitting in front of the current event router. It will run a two-stage validation: 1) structural contract linting (fast, schema-level checks) using precompiled JSON-LD/JSON Schema rules; 2) optional semantic rules executed in a sandboxed WASM engine for slower but more expressive invariants (e.g., field co-occurrence, enum folding).

Key components: 
- Admission controller HTTP layer with throttling and token-aware routing.
- Contract Linter: compiled rule bundles (versioned) fetched from config store.
- WASM executor: sandboxed, memory-limited runtime with timeouts per invocation.
- Leniency strategy: policy engine that marks events as REJECT | LENIENT_ACCEPT | ACCEPT based on rule severity, historical telemetry, and per-customer config.
- Telemetry & Tracing: structured logs, OpenTelemetry spans, and metrics exported to Console observability.
- Rollout: feature-flagged per-organization, with canary percentage and automatic rollback on error spike.

Trade-offs considered:
- Synchronous validation increases tail latency; mitigations: compile rules, warm WASM pools, and run semantic checks asynchronously with a fast-path structural gate.
- Holding back incompatible events may hide customer problems temporarily; lenient_accept preserves data while marking for downstream review.
